None of the devoted things may stick to your hands, so that the LORD may turn from his burning anger, show you mercy, have compassion on you, and make you many, as he swore to your ancestors, if you obey the LORD your God by keeping all his commandments that I am giving you today and doing what is right in the sight of the LORD your God.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 14
fields.body_html:
Children of the LORD

You are children of the LORD your God. Do not gash yourselves or shave a bald patch on your foreheads in mourning for the dead. For you are a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God. Out of all the peoples on the face of the earth, the LORD has chosen you to be his own special treasure.

Clean and unclean food

Do not eat anything detestable. These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat, the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep. You may eat any animal that both chews the cud and has a hoof split fully into two. Yet you must not eat these, even though they chew the cud or have split hooves: the camel, the hare and the rock badger. They chew the cud but do not have split hooves, so they are unclean for you. The pig has split hooves but does not chew the cud; it is unclean for you. Do not eat any of their meat, and do not touch them when they are dead.

Among the creatures of the water, any that have fins and scales are yours to eat. But do not eat anything without fins and scales; it is unclean for you.

You may eat any clean bird. But these are the ones you must not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture, the red kite, the black kite, the various kinds of kite, every kind of raven, the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, the various kinds of falcon, the little owl, the eagle owl, the barn owl, the desert owl, the carrion vulture, the cormorant, the stork, the various kinds of heron, the hoopoe and the bat. All winged swarming creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten. But you may eat any clean winged creature. Do not eat anything that has died on its own. The outsider living in your towns may have it to eat if you give it to them, or a foreigner may buy it from you. For you are a people set apart as holy to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.

The yearly tithe

Year after year, be sure to set aside a tithe of all the crops that grow from the seed you sow in the field. Eat it before the LORD your God, in the place he chooses as a dwelling for his name: the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks. In this way you will learn to fear the LORD your God at all times. If the journey is too long for you and you cannot carry it, because the place where the LORD your God chooses to put his name is too far from you, when the LORD your God has blessed you with plenty, then turn it into money. Tie up the money and carry it with you to the place the LORD your God chooses. Spend the money on whatever you wish: cattle, sheep, wine, beer, or anything else you would like. Then eat there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice, you and your household. And do not neglect the Levite living in your towns, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.

The tithe of the third year

At the end of every third year, bring out the whole tithe of that year’s produce and store it in your towns. Then the Levite, who has no portion or inheritance among you, and the outsider, the fatherless and the widow who live in your towns may come and eat until they are full, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work you do.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 15
fields.body_html:
The release of debts

At the close of every seven years you are to grant a release of debts. This is how the release is to be done: every creditor is to let go of what he has lent to his neighbor. He must not press his neighbor, his fellow Israelite, for payment, because a release in honor of the LORD has been proclaimed. You may press a foreigner for payment, but whatever your fellow Israelite owes you, you must release. Yet there will be no one in need among you, for the LORD will surely bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, provided that you listen closely to the voice of the LORD your God and carefully keep this whole commandment I lay on you today. For the LORD your God will bless you, as he promised you. Many nations will borrow from you, and you will borrow from none; many nations will be under your rule, and none will rule you.

Open your hand to the poor

If one of your fellow Israelites in one of your towns, in the land the LORD your God is giving you, falls into need, do not harden your heart or keep your hand closed against that needy person. Instead, open your hand to him generously and lend him as much as he needs to meet his want. Be on your guard against a base thought in your heart, such as, ‘The seventh year, the year of release, is close,’ so that you look grudgingly at your needy fellow Israelite and give him nothing. He may cry out to the LORD against you, and the sin will be counted against you. Give to him freely, and do not be sorry in your heart as you give. For this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in every task you take up. For the needy will never be gone from the land. So I command you: open your hand freely to your brother, to the poor and needy among your people in your land.

Setting slaves free

If a fellow Hebrew, a man or a woman, is sold to you as a slave and serves you six years, then in the seventh year you must send that person away free. When you set him free, do not let him go with empty hands. Load him generously with gifts from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress. Give him a share of what the LORD your God has blessed you with. Keep in mind that you yourself were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you. This is the reason for the command I give you today. But if he tells you, ‘I will not go away from you,’ because he loves you and your household and life with you is good for him, then you are to take an awl and pierce his ear with it, right into the door; he will then be your slave for life. Treat your female slave in the same way. Do not take it hard when you let him go free. His six years of service have been worth double a hired worker’s wages. And the LORD your God will bless you in all you do.

Firstborn animals

Every firstborn male born in your herd and your flock is to be made holy to the LORD your God. You must not work the firstborn of your cattle or shear the firstborn of your flock. Year after year, at the place the LORD will choose, you and your household are to eat it before the LORD your God. But if it is flawed in any way, lame or blind or with any other serious defect, it is not to be sacrificed to the LORD your God. Eat it in your own towns. Anyone, unclean or clean, may eat it, just as with gazelle or deer. Only, you must not eat its blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 16
fields.body_html:
The Passover

Observe the month of Abib by keeping the Passover for the LORD your God, because it was in the month of Abib, at night, that the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt. Sacrifice the Passover to the LORD your God, from your flock or your herd, at the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for his name. Do not eat bread made with yeast with it. For seven days eat bread made without yeast with it, the bread of affliction, because you left the land of Egypt in a hurry. Do this so that all your life you will remember the day you came out of the land of Egypt. For seven days no yeast is to be seen anywhere in your land. And none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day may be left over until morning. You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the towns the LORD your God is giving you, but only at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name. There you are to sacrifice the Passover in the evening, as the sun goes down, at the time of day you came out of Egypt. Cook it and eat it at the place the LORD your God will choose. Then in the morning turn back and go to your tents. For six days eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day hold a solemn assembly for the LORD your God. Do no work on it.

The Festival of Weeks

Count seven weeks. Begin counting the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain. Then keep the Festival of Weeks for the LORD your God, bringing a freewill offering from your own hand, as much as fits the way the LORD your God has blessed you. Rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, the Levite who lives in your towns, and the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow who live among you. Rejoice at the place the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name. Remember that you were slaves in Egypt, and be careful to keep these statutes.

The Festival of Booths

Keep the Festival of Booths for seven days, when you have gathered in the harvest from your threshing floor and your winepress. Rejoice at your festival, you and your son and daughter, your male and female servants, and the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow who live in your towns. For seven days keep the festival for the LORD your God at the place the LORD will choose. For the LORD your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all that your hands do, and you are to be nothing but joyful. Every male among you is to appear before the LORD your God three times a year, at the place he will choose. The three times are the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Booths. None of them is to come before the LORD with empty hands. Each of them is to give as he is able, in keeping with the blessing the LORD your God has given you.

Judges and justice

Appoint judges and officials for each of your tribes in all the towns the LORD your God is giving you, and they are to judge the people with fair judgment. Do not bend justice, and do not favor anyone because of who they are. Take no bribe, for a bribe makes even the wise blind and overturns the pleas of those in the right. Pursue what is right, nothing but what is right, so that you may live and take possession of the land the LORD your God is giving you.

Do not plant any tree as an Asherah pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God.

And do not set up a standing stone, a thing the LORD your God hates.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 17
fields.body_html:
Do not sacrifice an ox or a sheep or goat to the LORD your God if it has a defect or anything wrong with it, because that is detestable to the LORD your God.

Doing evil among you

If a man or a woman is found among you, in one of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you, doing what is evil in the sight of the LORD your God and breaking his covenant, who has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the stars in the sky, which I have not commanded, and you are told about it, then you must investigate it carefully. If it is true and the charge is proved that this detestable thing has been done in Israel, then you are to bring out to your town gates the man or the woman who has done this evil thing, and stone that person to death. A person may be put to death only when two or three witnesses give evidence. The word of one witness is not enough to put anyone to death. The witnesses must be the first to raise their hands to put that person to death, and then all the people are to join in. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.

Cases too hard to decide

If a case is too hard for you to decide, whether it concerns bloodshed, legal claims or injuries, any kind of dispute in your towns, then you are to set out and go up to the place the LORD your God will choose, and go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Ask them about the case, and they will give you the verdict. Then carry out the verdict they announce to you there, at the place the LORD will choose. Take care to follow all their directions exactly. Act on the instruction they give you and the ruling they announce to you. Do not turn aside from the verdict they declare to you, either to the right or to the left. Anyone who arrogantly refuses to listen to the priest who stands there serving the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. In this way you will remove the evil from Israel. All the people will hear of it and be afraid, and they will not act arrogantly again.

When you set a king over you

Once you have entered the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and you have taken possession of it and are living there, if you then say, ‘Let us appoint a king over us, like all the nations that surround us,’ you may indeed set a king over you, but it must be the one the LORD your God chooses. Set over you a king from among your fellow Israelites; you may not put a foreigner over you, someone who is not one of your own people. But he must not build up a large number of horses for himself, or send the people back to Egypt to get more horses, for the LORD has told you, ‘You must never go back that way again.’ He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will be led astray. And he must not pile up great amounts of silver and gold for himself. When he takes his seat on the throne of his kingdom, he is to write out for himself a copy of this law on a scroll, from the one kept by the Levitical priests. He must keep it with him and read from it all his life, so that he learns to fear the LORD his God, carefully keeping every word of this law and these statutes and doing them, so that he does not think himself above his fellow Israelites or stray from the commandment to the right or the left. Then he and his descendants will reign over his kingdom in Israel for a long time.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 18
fields.body_html:
The portion of the priests and Levites

The Levitical priests, and indeed the whole tribe of Levi, will receive no portion and no inheritance alongside Israel. They will eat from the food offerings of the LORD, since these are their inheritance. Among the other tribes Levi will own nothing as an inheritance; the LORD is his inheritance, as he told him.

This is what the priests are owed by the people who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they are to give the priest the shoulder, the jaws and the stomach. Give him as well the first of your grain, of your new wine and of your olive oil, and the first wool your sheep yield at shearing. Out of all your tribes it is he whom the LORD your God has chosen, he and his sons, to stand and serve in the name of the LORD for all time.

Suppose a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he has been living, and he comes because he longs with all his heart to go to the place the LORD will choose, he may serve in the name of the LORD his God just as all the other Levites do who stand there before the LORD. They are to eat equal shares, even if he has money from selling what came to him from his family.

Do not learn the ways of the nations

When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn from those nations to do the detestable things they do. No one among you is to make a son or daughter pass through the fire, or practice divination, or tell fortunes, or read omens, or practice sorcery, or cast spells, or consult a medium or a spiritist, or seek answers from the dead. The LORD detests anyone who does these things. It is for these detestable practices that the LORD your God is driving those nations out before you. You are to be blameless in your loyalty to the LORD your God.

A prophet like Moses

The nations you are about to dispossess pay attention to fortune-tellers and diviners. But the LORD your God has not allowed you to do the same. The LORD your God will raise up a prophet for you like me, one of your own fellow Israelites from among you. It is to him you must listen. It is what you requested from the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, ‘I must not hear the voice of the LORD my God again or look at this great fire any longer, or I will die.’ Then the LORD said to me, ‘They have spoken well. From among their fellow Israelites I will raise up a prophet for them who is like you. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will pass on to them all that I command him. If anyone does not listen to my words that the prophet speaks in my name, I myself will hold that person responsible. But a prophet who dares to speak a word in my name that I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die.’ You may wonder, ‘How are we to recognize a word that the LORD has not spoken?’ When a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and his word does not happen or come true, the LORD did not speak that word. The prophet spoke it presumptuously; do not be afraid of him.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 19
fields.body_html:
Cities of refuge

When the LORD your God has destroyed the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you have driven them out and settled in their towns and houses, you are to set apart three cities inside your land, the land the LORD your God is giving you to take as your own. Prepare the roads, and divide into three regions the territory the LORD your God is giving you as your inheritance. Then anyone who has killed someone can flee to one of these cities. This is the rule for the killer who may flee there and stay alive: it is anyone who kills a neighbor by accident, without having hated that neighbor before. For example, someone goes into the forest with a neighbor to cut wood. As the ax is swung to fell a tree, the head flies off the handle and strikes the neighbor, who dies. The one who was cutting may flee to one of these cities and stay alive, or else the avenger of blood, in the heat of anger, might chase the killer, catch up because the way is long, and kill them. Yet that person did not deserve to die, having had no hatred for the dead neighbor before. That is why I command you to set apart three cities.

If the LORD your God extends your borders, as he promised your ancestors on oath, and gives you all the land he said he would give them, because you are careful to keep this whole commandment that I give you today, to love the LORD your God and to walk always in his ways, then add three more cities to these three, so that innocent blood is not shed in the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you do not become guilty of bloodshed.

But if someone hates a neighbor, lies in wait, attacks and kills that neighbor, and then flees to one of these cities, the elders of the murderer’s own town are to send for them, bring them back from there and hand them over to the avenger of blood to be put to death. Show them no pity. You must remove from Israel the guilt of innocent blood, so that it may go well with you.

Boundary markers and witnesses

Do not move your neighbor’s boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you will receive in the land the LORD your God is giving you as your own.

One witness alone is not enough to convict anyone of any crime or wrong, whatever the offense may be. A case can stand only on the evidence of two or three witnesses. If a witness who means harm comes forward to accuse someone of wrongdoing, then the two people who have the dispute must stand before the LORD, in front of the priests and the judges in office at that time. The judges are to look into the matter carefully. If the witness proves to be a liar who has given false evidence against a fellow Israelite, do to that witness what the witness intended to do to the other person. In this way you will remove the evil from among you. Everyone else will hear of it and be afraid, and none of them will ever again do anything so evil among you. Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 20
fields.body_html:
Going out to battle

When you march out to battle against your enemies and face horses and chariots and a force bigger than your own, do not fear them. The LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you. As you approach the battle, the priest is to step forward and speak to the troops. He shall say to them, ‘Hear, Israel: today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, do not panic, and do not shrink back in terror before them, for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will fight for you against your enemies and give you victory.’ Then the officials are to say to the troops, ‘Has anyone built a new house and not yet dedicated it? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else dedicate it. Has anyone planted a vineyard and not yet begun to enjoy its fruit? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else enjoy it. Has anyone become pledged to a woman and not yet married her? He should go back home, or he may die in battle and someone else marry her.’ The officials are to go on to say to the troops, ‘Is anyone afraid or fainthearted? He should go back home, so that he does not make his fellow soldiers lose heart as he has.’ When the officials have finished speaking to the troops, they are to appoint commanders of the divisions to lead them.

Attacking a city

When you march up to a city to attack it, first offer it terms of peace. If it accepts your offer of peace and opens its gates to you, then all the people in it are to become forced laborers for you and serve you. But if it refuses to make peace with you and fights against you, lay siege to it. When the LORD your God hands it over to you, put all its men to the sword. But the women, the children, the livestock and everything else in the city, all its spoil, you may carry off as plunder for yourselves. You may use the spoil of your enemies, which the LORD your God has given you. This is how you are to deal with all the cities that are very far from you, the ones that do not belong to the nations here. But in the cities of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, do not leave alive anything that breathes. You must devote them completely to destruction, the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, just as the LORD your God commanded you, so that they will not teach you to copy all the detestable practices they have carried out for their gods, and so lead you to sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a city for a long time, fighting against it to take it, do not destroy its trees by taking an ax to them. You may eat their fruit; do not cut them down. Is a tree in the field a person, that you should besiege it as well? Only the trees that you know do not give food may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the city that is at war with you, until it falls.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 21
fields.body_html:
When someone is found slain

If someone is found slain, lying in the open country in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to take possession of, and no one knows who struck the victim down, your elders and your judges are to go out and measure the distance from the body to each of the towns around it. The elders of the town nearest the body are to take a heifer from the herd that has never been put to work and has never pulled in a yoke. The elders of that town are to lead the heifer down to a valley with a stream that never runs dry, on land that is neither plowed nor sown, and there in the valley they are to break the heifer’s neck. The priests, the sons of Levi, are to step forward. The LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to pronounce blessings in the name of the LORD, and their word is to settle every dispute and every case of assault. Then all the elders of the town nearest the body are to wash their hands in the valley over the heifer whose neck was broken. They are to declare, ‘Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it done. Make atonement for your people Israel, whom you redeemed, LORD, and do not hold the guilt of innocent blood against your people Israel.’ Then the bloodshed will be atoned for on their behalf. In this way you will purge the guilt of innocent blood from among you, for you will be doing what is right in the sight of the LORD.

Women taken captive

When you go out to war against your enemies and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take some of them captive, and you see among the captives a beautiful woman whom you desire and want to marry, you are to bring her into your home. She is to shave her head, trim her nails, and take off the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She is to stay in your house and mourn for her father and mother a full month. After that you may sleep with her and be her husband, and she will be your wife. But if you are no longer pleased with her, you are to let her go free wherever she wishes. You must never sell her for money or treat her as a slave, because you have dishonored her.

The right of the firstborn

If a man has two wives, one he loves and one he does not, and both have borne him sons, but the firstborn son is the son of the unloved wife, then when he divides his property among his sons as their inheritance, he must not give the rights of the firstborn to the son of the wife he loves in place of the son of the unloved wife, who is the true firstborn. He must acknowledge the son of the unloved wife as the firstborn by giving him a double share of all he has. That son is the first sign of his father’s strength, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.

A stubborn and rebellious son

Suppose a man has a son who is stubborn and rebellious, who will not obey his father or his mother and will not listen to them even when they discipline him, his father and mother are to seize him and bring him out to the elders of his town, to the gate of the place where he lives, They are to say to the elders of his town, ‘This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard.’ All the men of his town are then to stone him to death. You must purge the evil from among you; all Israel will hear of it and be afraid.

If someone has committed a crime that carries the death penalty and has been put to death, and you hang the body on a tree, you must not leave the body on the tree through the night. Be sure to bury it that same day, for anyone hung on a tree is under God’s curse. You must not make unclean the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 22
fields.body_html:
Your neighbor’s animals

If you see a fellow Israelite’s ox or sheep wandering loose, do not look the other way. Be sure to take the animal back to him. If the owner does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him. Do the same with a donkey or a cloak, or anything else a fellow Israelite loses and you find. You must not look the other way.

If you see a fellow Israelite’s donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not look the other way. Be sure to help him get it back on its feet.

A woman must not wear a man’s things, and a man must not put on a woman’s clothing, because the LORD your God detests anyone who does these things.

A bird’s nest by the road

If you happen to come across a bird’s nest beside the road, in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs in it and the mother bird sitting on the chicks or the eggs, do not take the mother along with her young. Be sure to let the mother go free, though you may take the young for yourself, so that things may go well with you and you may live a long life.

When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof, so that you do not bring guilt for a death on your household if someone falls from it.

Two kinds together

Do not sow your vineyard with a second kind of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeited to the sanctuary, both the crop you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard.

Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.

Do not wear clothing woven of wool and linen together.

Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap yourself in.

Charges against a bride

If a man marries a woman and sleeps with her, but then turns against her, and charges her with shameful behavior and ruins her reputation, saying, ‘This is the woman I married, but when I slept with her, I did not find evidence that she was a virgin,’ the young woman’s father and mother are to take the evidence of her virginity and bring it to the elders of the town at the gate. The young woman’s father is to say to the elders, ‘I gave my daughter to this man in marriage, but he has turned against her. Now he has charged her with shameful behavior, saying, “I did not find evidence that your daughter was a virgin.” But here is the evidence of my daughter’s virginity.’ Then they are to spread out the cloth in front of the elders of the town. The elders of that town are then to take the man and punish him, and fine him about 2 1/2 pounds of silver, which they are to give to the young woman’s father, because this man has ruined the reputation of a virgin of Israel. She is to remain his wife, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.

But if the charge is true, and no evidence of the young woman’s virginity is found, then they are to bring her out to the doorway of her father’s house, and there the men of her town are to stone her to death, because she has done an outrageous thing in Israel by being sexually immoral while living in her father’s house. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.

A married or engaged woman

If a man is caught sleeping with another man’s wife, both of them must die, the man who slept with her and the woman as well. In this way you will remove the evil from Israel.

If a young woman who is a virgin is engaged to a man, and another man meets her in the town and sleeps with her, you are to take both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them to death: the young woman because, though she was in the town, she did not cry for help, and the man because he dishonored another man’s wife. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.

But if the man comes upon the engaged young woman out in the countryside, and he overpowers her and rapes her, then only the man who did this must die. Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no sin that deserves death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him. He came upon her out in the countryside; the engaged young woman cried for help, but there was no one there to rescue her.

If a man comes upon a young woman who is a virgin and not engaged, and he seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are discovered, the man who slept with her must pay the young woman’s father about 1 1/4 pounds of silver, and she is to become his wife because he violated her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.

A man must not marry his father’s wife; he must not uncover the edge of his father’s garment.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 23
fields.body_html:
The assembly of the LORD

No man whose testicles have been crushed or whose penis has been cut off may enter the assembly of the LORD.

No one born of a forbidden union may enter the assembly of the LORD. None of their descendants may enter it, not even in the tenth generation.

No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD. None of them may ever enter it, not even in the tenth generation, because they did not come to meet you with food and water on your journey after you left Egypt, and because Moab hired Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Aram-naharaim, to put a curse on you. But the LORD your God refused to listen to Balaam. Instead the LORD your God made the curse a blessing for you, since the LORD your God loved you. Never seek a peace treaty with them or work for their prosperity, as long as you live as a people.

Do not detest an Edomite, for he is your relative. Do not detest an Egyptian, because you lived as a outsider in his land. The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.

Keeping the camp holy

When you go out and camp against your enemies, guard yourself against anything that is wrong. If any man among you is unclean because of an emission during the night, he must go outside the camp and not come inside it. Toward evening he is to bathe in water, and at sunset he may come back into the camp. Have a place set aside outside the camp, and go out there when you need to relieve yourself. Carry a digging tool among your gear, and when you squat outside, dig a hole with it, and then cover up your excrement. For the LORD your God moves about in your camp to rescue you and to hand your enemies over to you. So your camp must be holy, or he may see something indecent among you and turn away from you.

An escaped slave

If a slave has escaped from his master and taken refuge with you, do not hand him back to his master. Let him live among you, in the place he chooses in any one of your towns, wherever suits him best. Do not mistreat him.

No Israelite woman is to become a shrine prostitute, and no Israelite man is to become a shrine prostitute. Do not bring a prostitute’s earnings or the wages of a male prostitute into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, because both are detestable to the LORD your God. Do not charge a fellow Israelite interest, whether on money, on food, or on anything else that can be lent for interest. You may charge interest to a foreigner, but not to a fellow Israelite, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you set your hand to in the land you are entering to take possession of.

Vows and a neighbor’s harvest

When you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not put off paying it, for the LORD your God will certainly ask it of you, and you will be guilty of sin. But if you hold back from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin. Be careful to do what you have said, just as you freely vowed it to the LORD your God with your own mouth.

When you go into your neighbor’s vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you like, until you are full, but do not put any into a basket.

When you go into your neighbor’s field of standing grain, you may pick heads of grain with your hand, but do not take a sickle to your neighbor’s grain.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 24
fields.body_html:
Divorce and remarriage

Suppose a man marries a woman, but she does not please him because he has found something indecent about her, and he writes her a certificate of divorce, hands it to her and sends her out of his house, and she leaves his house and becomes the wife of another man, and the second husband turns against her too, writes out a certificate of divorce for her, puts it in her hand and sends her from his house, or if the second husband who married her dies, then her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife, since she has been made unclean. That would be detestable in the sight of the LORD. You must not bring sin on the land the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.

When a man has just married, he is not to go out with the army or have any other duty laid on him. He is to be free to stay at home for a year and give joy to his new wife.

Do not take a hand mill, or even its upper millstone, in pledge for a debt. That would be taking in pledge the very means a person lives by.

If anyone is caught kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating the victim as a slave or selling him, that kidnapper must die. You must purge the evil from among you. When a serious skin disease breaks out, take great care to do exactly what the Levitical priests teach you. Be careful to follow what I commanded them.

Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on your journey after you came out of Egypt.

Pledges and wages

When you lend your neighbor anything, do not go into his house to pick out what he will give you as security. Wait outside, and let the borrower bring the pledge out to you. If he is poor, do not go to bed with his pledge still in your keeping. Be sure to give the pledge back to him at sunset, so that he can sleep in his cloak and bless you. It will be counted as righteousness for you in the sight of the LORD your God.

Do not take advantage of a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether a fellow Israelite or an outsider living in one of the towns of your land. Give him his pay on the day he works, before the sun sets, because he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may call on the LORD against you, and the sin will be counted against you.

Parents are not to be put to death for their children, nor children for their parents. Each one is to be put to death only for their own sin.

The outsider, the fatherless and the widow

Do not deny justice to the outsider or the fatherless child, and do not take a widow’s cloak in pledge. Remember that you were slaves in Egypt and that the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you are harvesting your field and leave a sheaf behind by mistake, do not go back for it. Let it go to the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow. That way the LORD your God will bless all the work of your hands. When you knock the olives from your trees, do not go back over the branches a second time. What is left is for the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow.

When you pick the grapes in your vineyard, do not go over it again for what remains. That is for the outsider, the fatherless child and the widow. Remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 25
fields.body_html:
No more than forty strokes

Suppose two people have a dispute and go to court, and the judges decide the case, declaring the one who is in the right innocent and the one who is in the wrong guilty. If the guilty person deserves to be beaten, the judge is to make him lie down and have him flogged in his presence with the number of strokes his offense deserves. He may be given up to forty strokes, but no more. If he were beaten with many more strokes than that, your fellow Israelite would be degraded in your sight.

You must not muzzle an ox when it is treading out grain.

A brother’s widow

When brothers live together on the family land and one of them dies without a son, his widow must not be married to someone outside the family. Instead, her husband’s brother shall marry her and so do for her the duty of a husband’s brother. The first son she bears shall bear the dead brother’s name, so that the dead man’s name is not wiped out from Israel. But if the man is unwilling to marry his brother’s widow, she shall go up to the elders at the town gate and say, ‘My husband’s brother refuses to keep his brother’s name alive in Israel. He will not do the duty of a husband’s brother for me.’ Then the elders of his town are to summon him and speak with him. If he holds to his refusal and says, ‘I do not want to marry her,’ then his brother’s widow is to go up to him in front of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot and spit in his face. She shall then declare, ‘So it shall be done to any man who refuses to build up his brother’s family.’ And his family will be known in Israel as ‘The family of the man whose sandal was pulled off.’

If two men are fighting each other and the wife of one of them comes up to rescue her husband from the man who is hitting him, and she reaches out and grabs the other man by his private parts, then you must cut off her hand. Show her no pity.

Honest weights and measures

You must not carry two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.

You must not keep two different grain measures in your house, one large and one small. You must have weights that are complete and honest, and measures that are complete and honest, so that you may live long in the land the LORD your God is giving you. For the LORD your God detests anyone who does such things, anyone who acts dishonestly.

Remember Amalek

Remember what Amalek did to you on your journey out of Egypt, how they met you on the road when you were tired and worn out and struck at your rear, cutting down all who were lagging behind. They had no fear of God. So when the LORD your God has given you rest from all the enemies around you in the land the LORD your God is giving you to possess as an inheritance, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under the heavens. Do not forget.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 26
fields.body_html:
The first fruits

When you have come into the land the LORD your God is giving you for an inheritance, and have taken possession of it and settled in it, take some of the first of every crop the ground produces, which you gather from the land that the LORD your God is giving you. Put it in a basket and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name. Go to the priest who is in office at that time and say to him, ‘Today I declare to the LORD your God that I have come into the land the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us.’ The priest will take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of the LORD your God. Then you shall speak up and declare before the LORD your God: ‘My ancestor was an Aramean, a wanderer. He went down to Egypt and lived there as a foreigner, few in number, and there he became a great nation, strong and numerous. But the Egyptians mistreated us and oppressed us, and forced hard labor on us. Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our cry and saw our misery, our toil and our oppression. The LORD brought us out of Egypt by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, by great terror, and by signs and wonders. He led us to this place and gave us this land, a land that flows with milk and honey. And now here I have brought the first of the produce of the ground that you, O LORD, have given me.’ Then set it down before the LORD your God and bow down in worship before the LORD your God. And you shall rejoice in all the good things that the LORD your God has given to you and your household, you together with the Levite and the outsider living among you.

The tithe of the third year

When you have finished setting aside the full tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless and the widow, so that they can eat their fill in your towns, then say in the presence of the LORD your God: ‘I have removed the holy portion from my house and have given it to the Levite, the outsider, the fatherless and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not turned aside from any of your commandments, and I have not forgotten them. I have not eaten any of it while in mourning, I have not removed any of it while I was unclean, and I have not given any of it for the dead. I have done what the LORD my God said; I have done all that you commanded me. Look down from heaven, your holy dwelling place, and bless Israel, your people, and the land you have given us, as you promised on oath to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.’

His treasured possession

Today the LORD your God commands you to keep these statutes and rulings. Be careful to keep them with all your heart and with all your soul. Today you have declared that the LORD is your God, and that you will follow his ways, keep his statutes, commandments and rulings, and listen to his voice. And today the LORD has declared that you are his people, his treasured possession, as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commandments, and that he will set you high above all the nations he has made, to be praised, famous and honored, and that you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised.”

fields.title: Deuteronomy 27
fields.body_html:
Stones and an altar on Mount Ebal

Moses and the elders of Israel gave the people this command: “Keep the whole commandment that I am giving you today. On the day you cross the Jordan into the land the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster. When you have crossed over, write on them every word of this law, so that you may enter the land the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, promised you. When you have crossed the Jordan, put these stones up on Mount Ebal and coat them with plaster, as I command you today. Build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use any iron tool on them. Use uncut stones to build the altar of the LORD your God, and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God. Sacrifice peace offerings, eat them there, and rejoice in the presence of the LORD your God. And write on the stones all the words of this law, very clearly.”

Today you have become the people of the LORD

Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel: “Be still and listen, Israel! Today you have become the people of the LORD your God. So obey the LORD your God and carry out his commandments and statutes that I am giving you today.”

The curses from Mount Ebal

On that day Moses gave the people this command: “When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin. And these tribes are to stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali. Then the Levites are to call out in a loud voice to all the people of Israel:

‘Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast idol, a thing the LORD detests, the work of a craftsman’s hands, and sets it up in secret.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who dishonors their father or mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who moves their neighbor’s boundary marker.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who denies justice to the outsider, the fatherless, or the widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his father’s wife, for he has violated his father’s marriage.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his sister, whether she is his father’s daughter or his mother’s daughter.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who strikes down their neighbor in secret.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

‘Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amen.’

fields.title: Deuteronomy 28
fields.body_html:
Blessings for obeying

If you truly obey the LORD your God and carefully keep all his commandments that I am giving you today, the LORD your God will raise you high above every nation on earth. All these blessings will come on you and catch up with you, if you obey the LORD your God. You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the countryside. Blessed will be the children you bear, the harvest of your soil and the young of your livestock, the young of your cattle and your sheep. Blessed will be your basket and your kneading bowl. You will be blessed as you come in and blessed as you go out. the LORD will let you defeat the enemies who rise up against you. They will march out against you by one road and flee from you by seven. the LORD will command blessing to be with you in your barns and in everything you set your hand to. He will bless you in the land the LORD your God is giving you. the LORD will make you a people holy to himself, as he promised you on oath, as long as you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and follow his ways. Then every people on earth will see that you bear the name of the LORD, and they will be afraid of you. the LORD will give you plenty of good things: many children, many young among your livestock and rich harvests from your soil, in the land the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you. the LORD will open for you the heavens, his rich storehouse, to send rain on your land at the right time and to bless all that your hands do. You will lend to many nations and borrow from none. the LORD will make you the head, never the tail; you will always be at the top and never at the bottom, if you heed the commandments of the LORD your God that I am giving you today and carefully keep them, and if you do not turn from any of the words I am giving you today, either to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and serve them.

Curses for not obeying

But if you do not obey the LORD your God and carefully keep all his commandments and statutes that I am giving you today, all these curses will come on you and catch up with you. You will be cursed in the city and cursed in the countryside. Cursed will be your basket and your kneading bowl. Cursed will be the children you bear, the harvest of your soil, and the young of your cattle and your sheep. You will be cursed as you come in and cursed as you go out. the LORD will send on you curse, panic and frustration in everything you set your hand to, until you are destroyed and quickly perish, because of the evil you have done in forsaking me. the LORD will make disease cling to you until he has wiped you out from the land you are entering to take possession of. the LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and the sword, with blight and mildew. They will hunt you down until you perish. The sky above your head will be bronze, and the ground beneath you iron. the LORD will turn the rain of your land into powder and dust; it will fall on you from the sky until you are destroyed. the LORD will let your enemies defeat you. You will march out against them by one road and flee from them by seven. You will become a thing of horror to all the kingdoms of the earth. Your dead bodies will be food for all the birds of the sky and the wild animals, and no one will frighten them away. the LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, scabs and itch that cannot be cured. the LORD will strike you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind. At noon you will grope like a blind person groping in the dark, and you will not succeed in anything you do. You will be nothing but oppressed and robbed all the time, and no one will come to save you. You will be engaged to a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house but not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but never enjoy its fruit. Your ox will be slaughtered in front of you, but you will eat none of it. Your donkey will be seized from you by force and never returned. Your sheep will be handed over to your enemies, and no one will come to save you. Your sons and daughters will be handed over to another people while you look on. Your eyes will wear themselves out longing for them all day long, and you will be powerless to do anything. A people you have never known will eat up the harvest of your soil and everything you have worked for, and you will be nothing but oppressed and crushed all the time. You will be driven mad by what you see with your own eyes. the LORD will strike your knees and legs with painful boils that cannot be cured, spreading from the soles of your feet up to the crown of your head. the LORD will bring you and the king you set over yourselves to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone. You will become an object of horror, a saying and a joke among all the peoples where the LORD drives you. You will take much seed out to the field but gather little, because locusts will devour it. You will plant vineyards and tend them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, because worms will eat them. You will have olive trees throughout your country but no oil to rub on your body, because your olives will drop off. You will have sons and daughters, but they will not stay with you, because they will be taken away as captives. Swarms of insects will take over all your trees and the crops of your land. The outsider living among you will rise above you higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower. He will lend to you, but you will have nothing to lend to him. He will be the head, and you the tail. All these curses will come on you. They will hunt you down and catch up with you until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the LORD your God by keeping the commandments and statutes he commanded you. They will be a sign and a warning against you and your descendants forever. Since you did not serve the LORD your God joyfully and with a glad heart when you had plenty of everything, you will serve the enemies the LORD sends against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and in need of everything. He will lay an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you. the LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle, a nation whose language you will not understand, a hard-faced nation that will show no respect to the old and no pity to the young, and it will eat the young of your livestock and the harvest of your soil until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine or olive oil, none of the young of your cattle or your sheep, until it has ruined you. It will besiege all your towns until the high, fortified walls you trust in come down throughout your land. It will besiege all your towns throughout the land the LORD your God has given you. Then in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings upon you, you will eat your own children, the flesh of the sons and daughters the LORD your God has given you. Even the most gentle and refined man among you will begrudge food to his own brother, to the wife he holds close and to the children he still has left, and will not give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing else left, in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings upon you in all your towns. The most gentle and refined woman among you, so delicate and pampered that she would never venture to put the sole of her foot on the ground, will begrudge food to the husband she holds close, to her son and to her daughter, and to the afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and to the children she bears. For she will eat them in secret, having nothing else at all, in the siege and in the distress your enemy brings upon you in your towns. If you do not carefully keep every word of this law written in this book, and do not fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God, then the LORD will strike you and your descendants with astonishing plagues, great and lasting plagues and severe and lasting sicknesses. He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you. the LORD will also bring on you every sickness and plague that is not written in this book of the law, until you are destroyed. Though you were as many as the stars in the sky, only a few of you will be left, because you did not obey the LORD your God. Just as the LORD delighted in doing you good and making you many, so the LORD will delight in making you perish and destroying you. You will be torn away from the land you are entering to take possession of. the LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known, gods of wood and stone. Among those nations you will find no rest, no place to rest the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you an anxious heart, eyes worn out with longing and a despairing spirit. Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will live in dread night and day, never sure that you will survive. In the morning you will say, ‘If only evening would come!’ and in the evening, ‘If only morning would come!’ because of the dread that fills your heart and the sights your eyes will see. the LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way I promised you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as slaves, men and women, but there will be no buyer.”

fields.title: Deuteronomy 29
fields.body_html:
The covenant in the land of Moab

These are the words of the covenant the LORD commanded Moses to make in the land of Moab with the Israelites, besides the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.

Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, “You yourselves have seen everything the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his officials and to his whole land, the great tests your own eyes saw, those great signs and wonders. Yet up to this day the LORD has not given you an understanding mind, seeing eyes or hearing ears. I led you for forty years in the wilderness. The clothes on your backs did not wear out, nor did the sandals on your feet. You ate no bread and drank no wine or beer, so that you would know that I am the LORD your God. Then you arrived at this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan marched out to fight us, but we defeated them. We took their land and handed it over to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh as their inheritance. So keep the terms of this covenant and do them, so that you will succeed in everything you do.

Standing today before the LORD

All of you are standing today before the LORD your God: the leaders of your tribes, your elders and your officials, all the men of Israel, your children, your wives, and the outsiders living in your camps, from those who cut your wood to those who draw your water, so that you may pass into the covenant of the LORD your God, and into the oath he is making with you today, in order to confirm you today as his own people, so that he will be your God, as he told you and swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath, but with those who are standing here with us today before the LORD our God, and also with those who are not with us here today. You yourselves know how we lived in Egypt and how we made our way through the nations along the route you took. You saw their detestable things and their idols of wood and stone, of silver and gold, that they had among them. Make sure there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe among you, whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God and goes off to serve the gods of those nations. Let no root grow among you that bears poison and bitter fruit. When such a person hears the words of this oath, they may congratulate themselves in their heart and think, ‘I will be safe, even though I follow my own stubborn heart.’ That would bring ruin on the watered land and the dry alike. The LORD will not be willing to forgive that person. Instead, the anger and jealousy of the LORD will burn like fire against them, and every curse written in this book will settle on them, and the LORD will wipe out their name from under heaven. The LORD will single them out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, in keeping with all the covenant curses written in this book of the law. In time to come your children, the generation who rise up after you, will speak of it, and so will foreigners who come from a distant land, when they see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses the LORD has struck it with, the whole land burned out with sulfur and salt, nothing sown, nothing sprouting, no plant coming up in it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, when the LORD overthrew them in his anger and fury, and all the nations will ask, ‘Why has the LORD done this to this land? Why this fierce and terrible anger?’ And the answer will be, ‘It is because they left the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, the covenant he made with them when he led them out of Egypt, and they went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods they had never known and that he had not given them. So the anger of the LORD burned against that land, and he brought on it every curse written in this book. The LORD uprooted them from their land in anger, fury and great wrath, and threw them into another land, as it is today.’ The hidden things belong to the LORD our God, but what has been revealed belongs to us and to our children for all time, so that we may do all the words of this law.

fields.title: Deuteronomy 30
fields.body_html:
Turning back to the LORD

When all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you, and you and your children turn back to the LORD your God and obey him with all your heart and with all your soul, doing all that I command you today, then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you. He will gather you again from all the peoples among whom the LORD your God has scattered you. Even if you have been driven out to the farthest edge of the sky, from there the LORD your God will gather you up, and from there he will take you back. The LORD your God will bring you into the land your ancestors took possession of, and you will take possession of it. He will make you more prosperous and more numerous than your ancestors. The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and so live. The LORD your God will lay all these curses on your enemies, the people who hate you and persecuted you. As for you, you will turn back and obey the LORD, and keep all his commandments that I am giving you today. The LORD your God will give you plenty in all that you do, in the children you bear, the young of your livestock and the crops of your soil, for your good. For the LORD will once more take delight in doing you good, as he took delight in your ancestors, if you obey the LORD your God and keep his commandments and statutes, as they are recorded in this book of the law, and if you turn back to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.

The word is very near you

For this commandment that I am giving you today is not too difficult for you, nor is it out of reach. It is not in heaven, that you would need to ask, ‘Who will climb up to heaven for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?’ Nor is it on the far side of the sea, that you would need to ask, ‘Who will cross the sea for us and get it for us, and tell it to us so that we can do it?’ No, the word is very near you, in your mouth and in your heart, for you to do.

Life and good, death and harm

See, today I have placed before you life and good, death and harm. For what I command you today is that you love the LORD your God, walk in his ways, and keep his commandments, statutes and rulings. Then you will live and grow numerous, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to take possession of. But if your heart turns away and you will not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them, I tell you plainly today that you will certainly be destroyed. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and take possession of. Today I call heaven and earth to testify against you: I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, that you and your descendants may live, by loving the LORD your God, obeying him and holding fast to him. For he is your life and your long years, so that you may live in the land that the LORD swore to give to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.”

fields.title: Deuteronomy 31
fields.body_html:
Joshua to go before the people

Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel. He said to them, “I am 120 years old today. I can no longer go out and come in before you, and the LORD has told me, ‘You will not cross this Jordan.’ The LORD your God himself is the one who will cross over before you. He will wipe out these nations in your path, and you will drive them out. Joshua too will cross over at your head, as the LORD has said. The LORD will deal with them as he dealt with Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings, and with their land, when he destroyed them. The LORD will hand them over to you, and you must deal with them exactly as I have commanded you. Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid of them or tremble before them, for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will not let you go, and he will not abandon you.”

Then Moses summoned Joshua and, with all Israel looking on, said to him, “Be strong and courageous. You are the one who will go with this people into the land the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance. The LORD himself goes ahead of you, and he will be with you. He will not let you go or abandon you. Do not be afraid or lose heart.” Then Moses put this law in writing. He handed it to the priests, the descendants of Levi, who were the bearers of the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all of Israel’s elders. Moses gave them this command: “At the end of every seven years, at the set time of the year of release, during the Festival of Booths, when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place of his choosing, you must read this law aloud to all Israel, so that they hear it. Gather the people together, men, women and children, and the outsiders who live in your towns, so that they may hear and learn, and fear the LORD your God, and carefully obey all the words of this law. Their children, who do not yet know it, will hear it too and learn to fear the LORD your God for as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of.”

Joshua commissioned at the tent of meeting

The LORD said to Moses, “The time of your death is near. Call Joshua, and the two of you come and stand at the tent of meeting, so that I can commission him.” So Moses and Joshua went and took their places at the tent of meeting. Then the LORD appeared in a pillar of cloud at the tent, and the pillar stood over its entrance.

Write down this song

The LORD said to Moses, “You are about to rest with your ancestors. Then this people will rise up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and break my covenant, which I made with them. On that day my anger will blaze against them. I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured. Many disasters and troubles will overtake them, and on that day they will say, ‘Have these disasters not come on us because our God is no longer with us?’ Yes, I will certainly hide my face on that day because of all the evil they have done in turning to other gods. So now write down this song for yourselves, and teach it to the Israelites. Put it on their lips, so that this song will be my witness against the Israelites. For when I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to give their ancestors, and they have eaten their fill and grown fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them. They will treat me with contempt and break my covenant. And when many disasters and troubles overtake them, this song will speak against them as a witness, because their descendants will not forget it. I know what their hearts are inclined to do even now, before I have brought them into the land I swore to give them.” So Moses wrote down this song that same day and taught it to the Israelites. Then the LORD commissioned Joshua son of Nun. He said, “Be strong and courageous. You are the one who will bring the Israelites into the land I swore to give them, and I will be with you.” When Moses had finished writing out the words of this law in a book, to the very last word, he gave this order to the Levites, the bearers of the ark of the covenant of the LORD: “Take this book of the law and set it next to the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. Let it stay there as a witness against you. I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive and with you, you have been rebelling against the LORD. How much more will you rebel after I am dead! Gather to me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I can speak these words for them to hear and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them. For I know that once I am dead you will become utterly corrupt and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. In days to come disaster will strike you, because you will do what is evil in the sight of the LORD and provoke him to anger by what your hands have made.” Then Moses recited the words of this song from beginning to end, while the whole assembly of Israel listened:

fields.title: Deuteronomy 32
fields.body_html:
The song of Moses

“Listen, heavens, and I will speak;
earth, hear the words I say.
May my teaching fall like rain,
my words settle like the dew,
like soft rain on young grass,
like showers on growing plants.
For I will proclaim the name of the LORD;
give our God the praise for his greatness!
The Rock: his work is perfect,
and all his ways are just.
A faithful God who does no wrong,
righteous and upright is he.
They have acted corruptly toward him; by their own fault they are not his children,
a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD,
you foolish and senseless people?
Is he not your father, who brought you into being,
who made you and set you firmly in place?
Remember the days of long ago;
think about the years of past generations.
Ask your father, and he will tell you;
ask your elders, and they will explain it to you.
When the Most High gave each nation its inheritance,
when he divided up humanity,
he fixed the borders of the peoples
according to the number of the Israelites.
But the LORD’s own portion is his people;
Jacob is the share he measured out as his inheritance.
He found him in a desert land,
in an empty waste where the wind howls.
He shielded him on every side and watched over him;
he guarded him as the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle that rouses its nest
and hovers over its young,
that spreads its wings to catch them
and carries them on its feathers,
The LORD alone led him;
no foreign god was at his side.
He set him riding over the heights of the land,
and he ate the crops of the fields.
He fed him honey from the crags
and oil from the hard rock,
curds from the cattle and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs, and rams of Bashan, and goats,
with the finest of the wheat;
and you drank wine, the foaming blood of grapes.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked out;
you grew fat, heavy and sleek.
He abandoned the God who made him
and treated the Rock of his salvation with contempt.
They made him jealous with foreign gods;
with detestable things they made him angry.
They sacrificed to demons that were not God,
to gods they had never known,
new gods who had recently arrived,
whom your ancestors never feared.
You neglected the Rock who fathered you;
you forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw it and rejected them,
because his sons and his daughters provoked him.
He said, ‘I will hide my face from them
and see what their end will be,
for they are a perverse generation,
children who cannot be trusted.
They made me jealous with what is no god
and angered me with their worthless idols;
so I will make them jealous with those who are no people
and anger them with a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled by my anger;
it burns down to the depths of Sheol.
It consumes the earth and its crops
and sets the roots of the mountains on fire.
I will pile disasters on them
and spend my arrows against them.
They will waste away from hunger, devoured by plague and deadly disease.
Against them I will send the teeth of wild animals,
and the venom of snakes that glide in the dust.
In the streets the sword will take their children,
and inside their homes terror will strike,
young men and young women alike,
the nursing baby and the gray-haired.
I would have said, “I will scatter them
and wipe out their memory from among humankind,”
but I feared the taunting of the enemy,
that their foes would misunderstand
and say, “Our own power has won;
it was not the LORD who did all this.”‘
For they are a nation without sense,
and there is no understanding in them.
If only they were wise, they would understand this
and see what their end will be.
How could one chase a thousand,
or two drive ten thousand away,
unless their Rock had sold them,
unless the LORD had surrendered them?
For their rock is not like our Rock,
as even our enemies must admit.
For their vine springs from the vine of Sodom,
from the fields of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are grapes of poison,
and their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is snake venom,
the deadly poison of cobras.
‘Is this not laid up in store with me,
sealed in my treasuries?
Vengeance is mine, and repayment,
for the time when their foot slips;
for the day of their disaster is near,
and their doom is rushing toward them.’
For the LORD will do justice for his people
and take pity on his servants,
once he sees their strength is spent
and no one is left, bound or free.
Then he will say, ‘Where are their gods,
the rock they ran to for shelter,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices
and drank their offerings of wine?
Let them get up and help you!
Let them be your shelter!
See now that I, even I, am he;
there is no god beside me.
I put to death and I bring to life; I wound and I heal,
and no one can rescue from my hand.
For I raise my hand to heaven
and swear: as surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword
and my hand grasps judgment,
I will take vengeance on my foes
and pay back those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood,
and my sword will eat flesh:
the blood of the slain and the captives,
the heads of the enemy’s long-haired leaders.’
Nations, shout for joy with his people,
for he will avenge his servants’ blood.
He will repay his foes with vengeance
and make atonement for his land and his people.”

It is your very life

Moses, together with Joshua son of Nun, came and recited the whole song for the people to hear. When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel, he said to them, “Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you today, so that you may command your children to be careful to do all the words of this law. It is no empty word for you; it is your very life. By this word you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess.”

Moses to die on Mount Nebo

On that very day the LORD said to Moses, “Climb Mount Nebo here in the Abarim range, in the land of Moab, facing Jericho, and look out over the land of Canaan, which I am giving the Israelites to possess. On the mountain you climb you will die and be gathered to your people, just as Aaron your brother, who died on Mount Hor, was gathered to his people, because both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, and because you did not treat me as holy among the Israelites. You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it, the land I am giving to the Israelites.”

fields.title: Deuteronomy 33
fields.body_html:
Moses blesses the tribes

This is the blessing that Moses the man of God pronounced over the Israelites before he died.
He said:
“The LORD came from Sinai and rose like the dawn on them from Seir;
he shone out from Mount Paran
and came from among myriads of holy ones;
from his right hand came a law of fire for them.
Truly he loves the peoples;
all his holy ones are in your hand.
They sit down at your feet,
and each receives your words.
Moses gave us a law to keep,
the inheritance of the assembly of Jacob.
So he became king in Jeshurun
when the leaders of the people assembled,
all the tribes of Israel together.
May Reuben live and not die out,
even though his men are few.

This he said of Judah:
Hear, LORD, the voice of Judah,
and bring him to his people.
He fights for his cause with his own hands;
be his help against his enemies.

Of Levi he said:
Your Thummim and Urim belong to your faithful one,
the man you tested at Massah,
with whom you strove at the waters of Meribah,
who said of his father and mother, ‘I have no regard for them.’
He would not acknowledge his brothers
or claim his own children,
for they kept your word
and guarded your covenant.
They teach your rulings to Jacob
and your law to Israel;
they set incense before you
and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
Bless his strength, LORD,
and be pleased with the work of his hands.
Crush the loins of all who rise against him and of those who hate him, so that they never rise again.

Of Benjamin he said:
The one the LORD loves lives in safety beside him;
he shelters him all day long,
and Benjamin rests between his shoulders.

The blessing of Joseph

Of Joseph he said:
Blessed by the LORD be his land
with the finest gifts of the sky, with dew,
and with the deep waters that lie below,
with the best that the sun brings forth
and the richest crops of every month,
with the finest yield of the ancient mountains
and the choicest gifts of the everlasting hills,
with the best gifts of the earth and all that fills it,
and the favor of him who dwelt in the bush.
May all this rest on the head of Joseph,
on the brow of the one set apart from his brothers.
In majesty he is like a firstborn bull; his horns are the horns of a wild ox.
With them he gores the peoples, all of them, to the ends of the earth.
Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim,
such are the thousands of Manasseh.

Zebulun, Issachar, Gad, Dan and Asher

Of Zebulun he said:
Rejoice, Zebulun, when you go out,
and you, Issachar, in your tents.
They will call peoples to the mountain,
and there they will offer right sacrifices;
for they will draw from the wealth of the seas
and the treasures hidden in the sand.

Of Gad he said:
Blessed is the one who gives Gad room to grow!
He lies down like a lion
and tears off arm and scalp.
He chose the best land for himself,
for a commander’s share was kept for him there.
He marched with the leaders of the people;
he carried out the justice of the LORD
and his rulings together with Israel.

Of Dan he said:
Dan is a lion’s cub
that springs out from Bashan.
Of Naphtali he said:
Naphtali, rich in favor
and full of the blessing of the LORD,
take possession of the lake and the south.

Of Asher he said:
Most blessed of the sons is Asher;
may he be the favorite of his brothers
and dip his feet in oil.
Your bolts will be iron and bronze,
and your strength will last as long as your days.
There is no one like God, Jeshurun,
who rides through the heavens to help you
and through the skies in his majesty.
The God of old is a refuge,
